fit_tips: Measure around the widest part of the ribcage, just behind the front legs. That number picks your size.
The harness should sit snug — two fingers under the strap, no more. Loose kit is the usual reason a dog slips out.
Run the belt through the loop on the back, not around the neck. Keep your dog in the back seat, facing forward.

specs.v: Small 5–10 kg · Medium 10–25 kg · Large 25–40 kg
10 mm closed-cell foam at chest and sternum

faq.a: It clips into any standard lap-and-shoulder seat belt, which covers essentially every passenger car made since the 1970s. It does not fit lap-only belts in the centre rear seat of some older cars.

faq.q: How do I know which size to order?
faq.a: Measure the widest part of the ribcage behind the front legs. Small is 5–10 kg, Medium 10–25 kg, Large 25–40 kg. If your dog sits between two sizes, go up — the straps adjust down but not past their limit.

faq.q: Can my dog still sit up and lie down?
faq.a: Yes. The tether is short enough to stop them reaching the front seats, and long enough to stand, turn and lie down on the seat.

faq.q: Is it safe in a crash?
faq.a: It is designed to hold your dog in place on the seat and to spread load across the chest rather than the throat. Be clear on the limit: like every harness sold without a crash-test certificate, we cannot claim a tested crash rating. It is far safer than an unrestrained dog, which is the comparison that matters most.

faq.q: What if it does not fit?
faq.a: Send it back within 30 days for a full refund, including the return postage. No form to fill in — reply to your order email.
